notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r18
notes.notes:
Content Changes:
Bugfix for environments without a power stat.

Renamed mana cells to mana gems.

Piles no longer have a critical difficulty stat (since you can't crit a pile).

The magic abilities that did physical damage now use standard power scaling (makes them stronger).

Hordes now have colors.

Fire mage path now has a weakness to fire ability (as do the elementalist and archmage paths).

Tweaked monster stats.

Bosses now get double their base horde stats (will probably make them a bit stronger; this replaced custom boss stats).
Innate Changes:
Some color fixes for terrain type in various modals.

Added new resource nodes that allow leveraging skills such as civilian mining to gather. (There currently aren't any examples in the demo.)

Text for scavenge to gather in zone object modal (supports new resource nodes).

Views and zone objects are now sorted alphabetically in the targets pane.

Views now combine comment and discovered comment (no more dupes, although I don't think it was obvious in-game).

The monster corpse devouring action now requires the same health type on monster and target.

Character info now shows "IsBoss" if it's a boss (and getting double stats).

The Escape key now closes windows.

The exp log now shows total progress to next level.

The level-up log shows total levels for that type of experience, as well as the current value of the stat.

Level-up logs now have a different color than exp logs.

Added an alert (!) to monsters with higher level than you. Added a tooltip going into detail on the alerts.

Bugfix for action on a view listing ???? as the view in the action summary.

This update shouldn't break saves. You'll need to start a new game to pick up content changes.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r17
notes.notes:
Content Changes:
Monster corpses no longer produce leather, and leather is no longer used in armor crafting. (This is due to a decision to not implement the Nexus room for early access release. The Nexus room idea was to provide a steady stream of monster corpses, so that if you relied on any component from them, you wouldn't be stuck if a new sector didn't have that kind of monster. I'd still like to implement the Nexus room, but I can't promise it.)

Disabled Nexus skill stats on player.
Innate Changes:
Combat NPCs will now prioritize closing rifts over looting corpses and repairing turrets.

Crafting supply bonus from crafting room level is now 10% of project supply value per level.

Set default monster level cap to 100 (I'd consider it "normal" difficulty).

Disabled Nexus logging on base (at rift conquering).

This update shouldn't break saves. You'll need to start a new game to pick up content changes.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r16
notes.notes:
Content Changes:
Strength now boosts physical resists, to replace max encumbrance.

Paths no longer boost max encumbrance.

Stunned and Shocked conditions now affect stats other than max encumbrance.

Jetpack flight buff now increases Evasion. Jetpack provides less ability power per level.

Rebalanced project supply to be less across the board: 10 for equipment, 20 for consumables, and 50 for ammo. Note this will innately increase prices.

The base now starts at half supply for all items.

Supply threshold for triggering projects now uses base supply gain (times item level).
Innate Changes:
Disabled the encumbrance/immobilized mechanic (and updated dialogs to match). Short version: it was frustrating on character create to pick proficiencies and not be able to use them, and at the same time, over the course of the game, encumbrance becomes trivial (it doesn't scale). Also, it was bit clunky in the background.

Disabled any kind of ability or profession check related to weight or encumbrance.

Added inline action expansion dialogs. If you click "Expand" on the drone, zone, or target panes, you get a much bigger pane for the action list, and you isolate the selected target. (Note that since there are no actions on rooms on base, the expand button is dimmed there.)

Added large, modal dialogs for drone, zone, and base logs. If you click "Full" on the relevant log, it will show the large version.

Bugfix for base not spending crafting supply from purchases (meant supply was never decreasing).

Bugfix for project tab shadow not resetting properly on new game load.

This update shouldn't break saves. You'll need to start a new game to pick up content changes.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r15
notes.notes:
Content Changes:
Moved magic bonuses from affinities to investiture, and halved the rate of accrual for most condition stats. Affinities are still important, since they're the proficiency stat for innate magical abilities, and they govern absorbing ambient mana. It should be harder, though, to stack condition boosts.

Path credit shop listings are no longer generated; paths will only be sold for prestige. Note this halves the available level progression in the demo; if that becomes an issue, I can add more path levels for prestige.
Innate Changes:
Adjusted presentation of difficulty settings to be more intuitive (unlimited monster levels is now at high end of difficulty options).

Added combat note on how power stats interact with damage.

Added option to autosave on exit, if needed (default is still not to autosave).

Capped usage exp tick magnitude to 10 times level. So, at level 2, you can at most pick up 20 usage exp in a stat per tick. (It was previously unlimited, so if you stacked enough, you could rapidly level usage exp, which could snowball.)

Added locations dialog, showing all wilds zones visited by the base.

The shop now has bars for each entry, which I hope will make it easier to read.

Credit and prestige purchases are now split into separate categories for items and mana.

Shop now has more credit exchange options (including max), and currency and protection panes should now be sized better.

Base log entries now have colors (mostly based on room), and drone item acquisition is noted specifically.

Drone logs about affecting the base now have base colors.

Bugfix for starting to create a character and then backing out and saving a game that's broken if you load it. (You now can't save until you start the game.)

This update shouldn't break saves. You'll need to start a new game to pick up content changes.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r14
notes.notes:
Innate changes:
The game should no longer crash on closing a rift, and a new teleporter should be created properly.

Added fullscreen window option to Options. It requires a restart. The bordered, maximized window is still default.

Productive scavenging, looting, and studying actions by the player report any changes to base in the drone log. This affects gathering resources to base and adding shop listings.

Cache discovery notice now added to scavenging action summary. (You already got equipment addition logs, just no explanation why.)

Completing the study of a zone object now unlocks its full comment, and also includes its comment in the action summary (like studying an item).

Bugfix for creating a new session, loading the path dialog, canceling the new game, loading an existing game, and leveling using the path dialog (it would zero your remaining mana, as if you were just starting the game).

Added a new difficulty dialog to the game creation process. Allows setting max level of monsters (and rifts) to 50, 100, 200, or unlimited. The default is still unlimited (very hard).

Added total rift levels and level cap information to world data (if loading an existing game, you'll need to progress one turn to see it).

This update shouldn't break saves, and shouldn't require starting a new game.

notes.title: Bugfix 0.9.1.4r13
notes.notes:
Some zone objects had broken study actions (they appeared as research, fabricate, etc). These should now be fixed.



This update shouldn't break saves, but you'll need to start a new game to pick up the change.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r12
notes.notes:
Content changes:
NPCs now have a chat flavor dialog in their action list. The dialog won't change over time, and doesn't cost turns to use. Some of the NPCs may be more helpful than others. :)

Did some renaming of characters, paths, and skills to be more thematic and shorter.

Did some more color work, mainly on projects (they have defaults now).

Bugfix for pistol ability proficiency (should be Firearms now).

Renamed the Power stat to Charge, to differentiate from the magic/physical/tech power stats.

Training for civilian skills no longer requires charge (since right now civilian NPCs have no way to restore it).

Adjusted exp requirements for spawner levels by 10x. This doesn't change how fast monsters level, but it will affect the level of new spawns. Overall, this should reduce the difficulty of the demo.
Innate changes:
Builders should now follow the construction priority queue order, instead of getting stuck in place on the Pylon. (Specifically, the queue determines what room gets upgraded next, if the resources are available, and a project isn't already started. Once a room upgrade project is started, the room then drops to the bottom of the queue. In practice, this means Builders will appear to be working mid-queue, but that's because mid-queue is where the oldest active upgrade project will usually be.)

Bugfix for NPCs not being able to purchase Lore-based stat levels. (This was causing flickering behavior, where an NPC would match for being able to shop, but then not be able to actually buy the thing to remove the flag, and so they'd bounce between shop and work.)

Zone labels now have a spotted enemy count, after the label. (Note that it may wrap.)

Zone labels now start with an "*" if unvisited by your base.

Fixed a couple text overruns for the drone log.

This update shouldn't break saves, but you'll need to start a new game to get the new content changes.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r11
notes.notes:
Changes:
In the shop, equipment is now split into weapons, armor, and accessories.

Weapons has tabs for primary and sidearm.

Armor has tabs for helmet, torso, gloves, and boots.

Accessories has tabs for back, amulets, and rings.

Path shop pane now has tabs for mana (which means all paths listed have a branch for that mana type).

Consumable shop pane now has tabs for restores, buffs, and attacks.

Stats shop pane now has tabs for skills, combat, and core.

Added colors to items, which should help distinguish them in the shop.

Modal panes will now resize width based on font size setting (should take care of horizontal text overruns). Also tweaked vertical a bit.

This update shouldn't break saves, though to pick up the color changes you'll need to start a new game.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r10
notes.notes:
Gameplay:
Combat NPCs now get a prestige salary every 5 turns. The salary is currently set to the level of the base. This should ensure that combat NPCs never get permanently stuck on base.


Information:
The leveling dialog now has toggles that set how many free points you add (or remove) in a single click. Default is still 1, but you can also set each type of free point to 5 or All.

The leveling dialog now has an actions-required pane, detailing what you need to do to highlight the execute button.

The Help screen is now a sorted display of all tool tip topics.



This update shouldn't break saves, and you shouldn't need to start a new game to pick up the changes.

notes.title: Update 0.9.1.4r9
notes.notes:
Gameplay:
Added three new combat NPCs to the demo: another Scrapper, an Investigator, and a Shielder.

Added shielder food to the cafe (increases shield proficiency).

Combat NPCs should no longer lose gear or mana on death. This is a quick fix to the problem of NPCs getting currency-locked to base, because they can't replace gear.

Reduced the combat NPC death fatigue penalty from 25 to 10.

Combat NPCs now reduce fatigue on base 2 per turn.


Bugfixes:
Consumable abilities should no longer be listed under player actions after a respawn without item protection.

Tweaked DB loading again to eliminate another bug.


Information:
Added experimental font size setting in options. Note that anything beyond 10% larger than normal seems to cause text overruns (though 20% isn't too bad).

Resource information now includes what base projects use the resource.

Project pane now has filter tabs.

Added some more notes on combat mechanics to the damage result modal tooltip.

Added note to selling tooltip about the ability to sell back to base at no loss.



This update shouldn't break saves, but you'll need to start a new game to pick up the new content.

notes.title: Gameplay and bugfix update 0.9.1.4r4
notes.notes:
Gameplay/content changes:
Chainsword abilities now cancel stealth on source (you still get one blindside attack).

Monsters now have a devouring skill to help consume corpses for exp (previously, they relied entirely on the Constitution stat, which was slow).

Monsters can now use the Rifting skill to help conquer rifts from other hordes.

The monster devour, grow, and tend actions can now be done while stealthed.

The Hammerer path now has all mana types unlocked, with magic hammer smash abilities for each type. The path also now provides a significant pierce boost to the mana type invested.

The Scrapper path now has all mana types unlocked, with magic chainsword slash abilities for each type. The path also now provides a significant steal boost to the mana type invested.

Rebalanced the dedicated magic paths to provide a significant power and resist boost, and removed the attribute boost. The second-order mage paths now also provide a significant pierce, steal, and reflect boost.

Added prismatic resist and power rings. Research is done at the Synergium, and crafting is done in the Accessories Factory.


Bugfixes:
Zone objects can no longer be blindsided.

Devour action for monsters now properly checks if it's doable.

Chainsword power type now matches abilities (tech power).

If any nested combo ability fails a check, it should now fail the whole combo.

The world database is refreshed on new game, which should prevent the issue of installing an update, loading an old game, and then starting a new game only to have the old saved database used to create the new game.

Combos done by the player should now log nested abilities to the player log, not the zone log.

Equipment-based path abilities should now pull proficiency type from the equipment, not the power class. (The magic weapon attacks granted by the Hammerer and Scrapper paths weren't using the hammer or power blades proficiencies like they were supposed to be.)

Zone object piles should no longer disrupt condition buff or debuff stacks if the pile changes level while affected by the condition.


Information changes:
Monster action results for things like devour no longer show skill exp (monsters don't get skill exp).

Profession action results now show speed where applicable.

Ability combos no longer display a power or effect class (since it's irrelevant; they're just a container for their nested abilities). 

Added a dialog for ability combo templates, so you can get data on them before choosing them.

The combo dialogs now show the targets of each nested ability.

Did some text/label changes.



This update should not break saves, but you'll need to start a new run to pick up the content changes.

notes.title: Bugfix 0.9.1.4r2
notes.notes:
Fixes:

The Repairing skill should now work for the player, and allow system exp levels.

Turrets killing the same enemy should no longer duplicate prestige kill awards.

This update shouldn't break saves, though a new game is needed to pick up the repairing changes.

notes.title: Gameplay Update 0.9.1.4r1
notes.notes:
Major changes:
Summon mechanic added. Summons have a max concurrent summons and a cooldown before another can be summoned. Kills made by a summon are credited to the summoner for purposes of awarding credits and prestige. Summons are persistent unless destroyed.

The Combat Engineer path now has summonable turrets for each mana type, depending on mana type invested in leveling.

Completing sector victory conditions no longer immediately stops gameplay. You may continue exploiting the current sector as long as you want. Note that in the campaign, I intend the base levels of future sectors to be augmented by total turns played, so there will be a cost to indefinitely exploiting a scenario. :)
Other changes:
Added a Rifter skill to help close rifts faster without needing to stack Wisdom. (Wisdom still helps.)

Added an Observer skill to do the same for views.

Added paths for Rifter, Observer, Scavenger, Lockpicker, Hacker, and Scholar. These advance the applicable skill, are a little stronger than civilian paths, though still not as strong as combat paths, and can be purchased in the shop. They are also unlocked by some combat paths.

Since DoTs are removed on base, I removed any DoT removals from the Medbay autodoc.

Monsters now free their spawner slot on death, not corpse decay. (This means more live monster time, overall.)

Fixed a bug with NPC behavior; should be improved.

Did some minor path and investiture rebalancing.

Wanderer and Combat Engineer paths now support all mana types.

Did some text/name improvements.

This update will break savegames!

notes.title: Bugfix and QoL update 0.9.1.3r5
notes.notes:
Changes:


 The health trainer now trains health as expected, not stamina.
 Service offers from the medbay now include a max based on either max needed, or max affordable, so to buy 100+ stacks of heals can now be done in one click. It also provides a range of static offers if applicable: 1x,  10x, 50x, and 100x.
 A minor text fix for the growth processing skill.


This update shouldn't break saves, though you'll need to start a new run to see the health trainer update.

notes.title: Bugfix update 0.9.1.3r2
notes.notes:
Fixes:
 
 It's now impossible to die on base (for any reason); your character will simply go negative on HP. (Leaving base would result in immediate death, but you shouldn't go negative HP on base: that would be a bug.)
 Vital death protection no longer preserves negative HP state, and instead restores HP to 1 if less than 1, and stamina, power, and calories to 0 if less than 0.
 If you are killed while moving to another zone and respawn at base, your character is no longer listed as arriving in the original target zone, and can no longer be sniped on base by remote monsters.
 Stamina syringes now restore stamina, not health. I also changed their value, so that small stamina syringes restore base 25, and normal restore base 50.


This update will break savegames.

notes.title: Bugfix
notes.notes:
Ending a demo run via loss or win should no longer prevent starting a new game in the same session. The issue was that the world interface state wasn't being cleared properly.

This update shouldn't break savegames, but it does include some new scenario handling code in preparation for campaigns. Here's hoping I didn't introduce a new critical bug. :)

Other changes include some minor text improvements (force field amulet project, and project unlock base logs), and a bugfix for monstrous growth stats not updating properly when leveling.

notes.title: Demo Release
notes.notes:
Overview

The free public demo is now available! Level your drone, kill monsters, scavenge resources, and clear the Dystopian refinery rift. :)

The demo is beta, but it has a lot of content and should provide a good idea of what the game is about. I intend to release updates for the demo, and I expect they’ll break savegames, so I’d recommend not installing an update unless you’re ready for a new run.

Unless there are serious bugs, I only intend to release an update once a week. I also have a public testing branch for the demo, and I may release updates more frequently there (and again, I’d assume they break savegames).

I have more balancing to do, and possibly more path content to add, but now that the demo is out, I want to start working on the campaign mechanics and campaign content, looking towards early access.

Ability Mechanics Additions and Changes

 Added magical and physical resistance buffs.
 Earth Touch can now break physical locks.
 Proficiency now applies to all boosts, including item ability stats.


Room Additions and Changes

 Balanced project supply, length, and thresholds.
 Rebalanced room ambience and mana gen (general increase).


Path Additions and Changes

 Added taunt ability and buff resist abilities to Shielder path.
 Added all mana types and attribute buff abilities to Pugilist path.
 Added mage shields to magic paths.
 Added additional earth armor physical defense buff to Earth Magic path.
 Rebalanced unarmed abilities (removed some duplicates for now, added Precision buff).
 Scrapper path now has a special chainsword-only ability that boosts damage, accuracy, and pierce with scavenging skill, and allows for fast scavenging.
 Most combat paths now grant some max encumbrance.
 Added stealth-breaking ability, and Dazzle debuff, to Light Magic path.
 Added Shadow Sense to Dark Magic path, which increases detection by area concealment.
 Added Analyze ability to Investigator path, which debuffs enemies, and can quickly study certain artifacts.
 Light and dark magic paths can unlock Investigator path levels.


Item Additions and Changes

 Added shield bash abilities to shields.
 Rebalanced armors to be stat-total-equal and more thematic; also added camouflage.
 Flashbang grenades no longer friendly fire.


Character Additions and Changes

 The teleporter now gets high detection, and an arcane wave AoE ability that breaks stealth.


Interface Additions and Changes

 Running projects are now sorted by name.
 The growing stage and harvest stage are now in different sections.
 Total temporary stat mods (like buffs and debuffs) are now color-coded in stat listings.
 Added an interface help screen, accessible from world interface.
 Save slot selection now defaults to first empty.
 Elevator list now shows zone colors, and allows right-clicking zones.
 Right-click dialog for possible player actions now shows power.
 Added background to main menu and other menus. Re-styled main menus and new game menus.
 Restyled path selection in the new game process; path options shows colors, and can be right-clicked for more details.
 Added more tooltips.
 Room information dialog now shows stat awards, base stat awards, shop stat awards, and shop path awards.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Overview

In this week's balancing and playtesting, I focused on various builds and playstyles, such as mage, wanderer, unarmed, medic, and submachine gun, and I added new items and abilities.

I also added resource extraction rooms and the player capability to purchase room construction levels for credits.

Looking forward to the demo release soon. :)

Demo Additions and Changes


 Added more buildings and items, like heavy weapons factory, energy weapons factory, gymnasium, library, and more.
 The studyable zone object artifacts in the world now provide shop stat listings. Path listings are found as looted items like books and data sticks. (Paths are more valuable, and the book/data loot is rarer.)


World Mechanics Additions and Changes


 Graffiti and other signs can no longer be directly scavenged. (Scavenging NPCs were destroying them before scholar NPCs could study them.)
 Scavenging and closing rift actions cannot be performed in stealth.


Ability Mechanics Additions and Changes


 Mage food no longer boosts affinity (due to an infinite recursive loop, where mage food would make the next application of mage food more powerful). Instead, it boosts specific magic stats that -don’t- do that. :)
 Detection Pulse is now a toggle, and requires goggles to be equipped.


Room Additions and Changes

 Credit cost for skipping resource requirements on projects now pays the total value of the resources (not an arbitrarily-defined value).
 Research, crafting, and refining projects now run in parallel (all possible projects are started in each room). NPCs will focus on the oldest running, but the player can choose what to advance.
 The base now splits credit income 50/50 between construction and crafting (since crafting projects are innately cheaper, they were soaking up all the credits).
 Removed prestige costs from training, since it was blocking combat NPCs without prestige. (I may adjust this later.)


Path Additions and Changes


 Mage paths now provide a choice each level between their “touch” attack and “bolt” attack. Every fifth level provides a choice between their “wave” attack and “blast” attack.


Shop Additions and Changes


 Paths and stat offerings in shop now sell based on innate value, regardless of source. (So, unlocking shop listings from artifacts and unlocking from room upgrades results in same costs.)
 Stat offerings can now be full levels. System stat listings take advantage of this (so every room level that unlocks another system stat purchase is in effect unlocking another possible stat level).
 Added regen stat listings. Max health, stamina, and power listings now provide +10 per purchase.
 Prices for items in shop now reflects actual supply cost. (Works out to be much cheaper and playable, I think.)
 You can now purchase construction projects for credits.
 Added extraction rooms: a mine, a quarry, and a swamp. These all provide raw materials that are refined into the materials used by the base to do room construction. They're slow, however; scavenging is a faster way to get resources. (The downside to scavenging is that it’s inconsistent.)
 Adjusted mana investiture to provide a bonus every fifth level as well as every tenth.


The construction shop:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/a92bb9f037f6c2f519b12fcc154cea18de1663b5.png

Item Additions and Changes


 Did a resource value balancing run.
 Added more permanent alchemical exp serums.
 Studying an artifact item provides a prestige award based on the value of the unlocked shop listing.
 Rebalanced weapon stats. Tech weapons that use ammo are among the most expensive combat abilities, and also are harder to scale with bonus stats, so I made their base stats higher. We’ll see how that works (I may also add more ways to boost tech weapon power).
 Added an injector weapon sidearm, that does toxin shots.
 The primary injector weapon can now do aerosol AoE attacks and buffs.
 The flashbang grenade can now break enemy stealth.
 Magic rods now provide an affinity and more power per level.
 Added sidearm cudgels for mages, that add some magic boosts (but not as much as rods).
 Added physical resist rings.
 Added the knuckles unarmed weapon crafting and research projects.


Character Additions and Changes


 Adjusted kill values, so you get more credits for a kill. Also, users contributing to a kill now get prestige.
 Made some AI changes to allow more diverse behaviors.
 Configured the Wanderer NPC around the concept of being in stealth and using stealth weapons (a crossbow and a sidearm toxin injector). Also provided the Wanderer path with hacking and lockpicking skill boosts.


Stat Additions and Changes


 Attribute training now uses relevant magic affinities as speed.
 Training now provides usage experience to speed stat.


Interface Additions and Changes


 Crafting project dialogs now link to the items they supply.
 Environment-applied conditions now show messages on condition resist.
 Teleporter health is now shown in the quests pane.
 Damage dialog now shows condition consumption boosts.


Other Additions and Changes

 Loading savegames now only works if the savegames are from the same version as the current build, otherwise, you get a version mismatch message. (New builds are expected to break savegames.)

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Overview

Did more demo playtesting and balancing. Getting very close now. :)

Demo Additions and Changes


 Populated more zone objects, artifacts, locked objects, and loot, including how-to mage guides, mana cells, data sticks with civilian profession boosts, weapons, consumables, armor, Dystopian safety posters, and more.
 Also populated discovered loot (which is loot you only get if you complete enough scavenges on a zone object).


World Mechanics Additions and Changes


 Looted resources go directly to faction storage, and provide a prestige award to looters based on value.
 Most discrete zone objects (like vehicles or machinery) are now studyable artifacts, requiring various civilian professions to study them. Rewards include max path levels and stat lore exp shop offerings.
 Discrete zone objects no longer add terrain difficulty; rubble piles do that instead. Discrete objects tend to add cover and concealment.


Ability Mechanics Additions and Changes


 Added a sniper rifle armor-piercing ability (and ammo).
 Combos now merge costs and cooldowns from all nested abilities. Cooldown is set to the longest.
 Users (including the player) can no longer use attacks that would result in friendly fire.
 Steal life should only work now if your health type is the same as the target’s health type (you can’t steal health from structures).
 Condition magnitude is no longer affected by zone ambience.


Path Additions and Changes

 Combat paths now include civilian skill boosts (this allows various combat NPCs to specialize in studying appropriate artifacts).
 The hammer path now has elemental hammer damage combos, that do both the basic weapon attack (with weapon stats) and an elemental attack.
 The primary magic paths now give you a choice per level among the four attack types: melee single, melee AoE, ranged single, and ranged AoE. Note that zone cover defends against both AoE and ranged, and zone concealment affects ranged single, generally making melee single the best chance to do damage.


Item Additions and Changes


 Weapons have stats again, and abilities that have equipment requirements check that equipment for any boosts. (This let me do the elemental hammer combo abilities, so that they leverage weapon level instead of ignoring it.)
 Added Dystopian serums, which increase the alchemical exp of a stat.
 Added scrap alloys resource, and a refining project to make alloys.
 Added new resist consumables, crafting projects, and source harvestable resources (aspected mushrooms, as well as hydroponics and terrarium resources).
 Added Boombadier Beetles and Death Centipedes harvestables to provide extracts used in making various kinds of ammo.


Character Additions and Changes


 Rats now decay into shadow bones (do ambient dark mana, not death).
 Monsters can now gain experience from ambient mana (based on affinity).
 Did some more specialization of monster orders, to vary their action patterns.


Stat Additions and Changes


 All stat exp ticks for users now check equipment to boost proficiency (unless it’s an equipment proficiency being ticked).

Interface Additions and Changes


 Improved ability result modal dialogs (especially damage). The information should be clearer.
 Did some color scheme tweaks.
 Added a zone log notification of day/night changes.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Overview

Did lots of demo content and rebalancing, with new zone objects, zones, a new hacking skill, rewards from unlocking views, and more. I'm very happy with the progress; I can see daylight on completing the demo, and I'm looking forward to building more scenarios afterwards. :)

Demo Additions and Changes


 Fleshed out the Administrative Office area (which effectively doubled the demo's size in zones).
 Reworked the refinery, rails, and pits area layout.
 Split existing areas, for more refined default environments.
 Since level matters more now, most monsters start at level one.
 Added more views.
 Added locked doors and computer terminals that leverage the new hacking skill.
 Added new objects like server racks, office chairs, garbage cans, wrecked cars, safety posters (you get lore exp for studying them), trash compactors, shredders, and more.


Zone Additions and Changes


 The cost of terrain movement and exploration is now reduced by terrain skill. The terrain difficulty sets the cost.
 Switched heaps of ore to heaps of rubble, and adjusted stats.
 Rebalanced stats for zone object material classes to be every X level (where appropriate).
 Added enchanted blast doors that resist magical as well as phsyical attacks. Must be hacked to be unlocked.
 Unlocking views can now add shop listings as rewards. So, a scenic vista might unlock lore experience for a terrain skill.


Spatial Base Additions and Changes


 The base now spends resources on projects before credits. Projects purchased for credits are no longer instantly completed; they must still be advanced by civilians.
 Teleporting home now preempts and prevents any incoming attacks.
 Teleporting home now clears all damage over time conditions.
 Room construction cost is now balanced to every X level (no up front spike and incremental increase).


Ability Mechanics Additions and Changes


 Hit mechanics now scale damage. Failing an accuracy check means doing half damage and no pierce. A normal hit does full damage and pierce, while a critical hit does double damage, pierce, and steal.
 Heals can now be set to “full heal”. In this case, heal power simply determines whether or not the heal occurs, and then the target stat is healed for its full value. Note that this can still result in less than 100% heal if the healed stat also gets its max buffed the same turn (since that’s procced after heals).
 Food and drink options in the cafeteria now do full heals.
 Persistent conditions now gain max stacks and stack accrual at the same rate.
 Added plasma and laser tech ability power classes. Plasma uses fire pierce and steal, and lasers use light pierce and steal.

 Did more ability stat balancing, to be per level, as opposed to a static up-front amount with incremental gains. So most level 2 abilities will be twice as powerful as their level 1 versions.
 Balanced damage and heal condition stats the same way.
 The Chilled condition now reduces stamina regen instead of depleting stamina over time. (Negative regen does not proc.)

Stat Additions and Changes

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Magic Additions and Changes

The basic abilities for the nine magic types are now divided as follows:


 Touch (melee single-target)
 Bolt (ranged single-target)
 Wave (melee AoE)
 Blast (ranged AoE)


Stats are modular. Touch is the most powerful, while range and AoE both reduce power somewhat. Cost follows the same pattern: touch is the cheapest, while range and AoE add cost.

Cost also has type: ambient mana vs internal mana. Ambient mana has cooldowns, which also obey the AoE and range expense pattern. Abilities that cost internal mana do not have cooldowns.

Each magic type now has its own bonuses:

 Fire has the most damage. It also gets a minor boost to condition damage and stack accrual. Its default damage condition is Burning, which does damage over time.
 Water has a minor pierce boost and a major boost to condition max duration and max stacks. Its default conditions are Frosted, which reduces evasion, agility, and water resistance, and Frostbite, a damage over time.
 Air gets minor damage, minor accuracy, and cheaper cost. It also gets Shocked, which reduces evasion, agility, and max encumbrance.
 Earth gets minor pierce, minor condition damage and accrual, and minor condition duration and stacks. It also gets Acid, which reduces physical resists and critical difficulty, and Corrosion, a damage over time. (I might switch those names.)
 Life gets minor condition damage and accrual, major duration and stacks, and Parasites, which reduces vitality and endurance.
 Death gets major condition damage and accrual, minor duration and stacks, and Decay, a damage over time.
 Light gets major accuracy, minor pierce, and cheaper cost. Light is split into two damage types, one for lasers that gets the Burning and Dazzled conditions, and one for radiation that gets damage over time and a debuff that reduces strength and constitution.
 Dark gets major steal, minor accuracy, and Shrouded, which reduces perception and dark resistance.
 Arcane gets major pierce, minor steal, and Disruption, which reduces all magic resists.


Ability Mechanics Additions and Changes

 Camouflage is now added to Evasion if defending against a ranged attack. Cover no longer provides this, but is still added to defense.
 Detection now pierces bonus evasion provided by Camouflage or Concealment.
 Added elemental attacks to the path of hammers: Fiery Smash, Frost Smash, Wind Smash, and Tectonic Smash.
 Condition resists now pull from the applying ability resist class. This let me remove the physical and tech condition resist stats (which I hadn’t used yet). The reason I did it differently at first was to allow an apply buff or debuff ability to be prismatic (apply both a fire and lightning debuff, for instance). Combo abilities now let me do that without issue.
 Buff and debuff power from apply abilities is now reduced by resists.
 Environments now pull resists from the environment resist class, and the power of afflicted conditions is reduced by those resists.


Path Additions and Changes


 Balanced the civilian and combat paths. A major difference is that at level 10, paths with multiple mana inputs now provide the mana levels needed to advance the path with any of the mana types. This is important for NPC leveling, since (right now) they don’t try to unlock new mana types, but stick to whatever they auto-unlock.


Character Additions and Changes


 NPCs now make auto-choices while leveling in world, for things like free stats and ability choices. (This was already working for initial levels.)


Other Additions and Changes

 Added an option to convert saves between JSON (cleartext) and binary (faster) formats.
 Added an option to switch between serial and parallel processing. (Serial is faster for now; apparently I haven’t scaled up enough monsters yet for parallel to be more efficient.)

notes.title: Weekly Update
Weekly Update
notes.notes:
World Mechanics Additions and Changes


 Characters now drop full inventory on death.
 Having more than max encumbrance triggers the Encumbered state, which doubles costs of actions (stamina and mana).
 More than double max encumbrance triggers the Immobilized state, which disables normal movement (flight may still be possible, and teleportation and elevator use still works). Immobilized also triples the costs of actions. Some other actions fail on this state, such as searching.


Ability Mechanics Additions and Changes


 The Stunned condition now increases encumbrance.
 The jetpack Flight ability now has a power-to-weight check, so you can only fly if ability power is greater than equipped item weight (which calcs before any proficiency encumbrance reductions). This means that if Flight has enough power, you can still move even if ordinarily immobilized.
 Added Ratbite Fever disease, a persistent condition that reduces max HP and increases resistance to beneficial life abilities (so it’s harder to heal).
 Added Cure Disease and Cure Wounds services to Medbay.
 Life steal is now capped to damage.
 Renamed hit difficulty to Evasion.
For non-AoE attacks, a hit is now determined by matching Accuracy to Evasion. Any leftover Accuracy is considered Critical Accuracy and then matched against Critical Difficulty to see if the hit is also a crit or even a massive crit (CritACC > CritDiff * 2). AoE attacks always hit, and do a guaranteed crit on the primary target (unless the zone itself is targeted).
 For non-AoE attacks, Accuracy usage exp is now based on Evasion if a miss, and on Critical Difficulty if a hit but not a crit. So, missing means you’re getting a lot of Accuracy exp, while hitting reduces that by quite a bit, and critting means no Accuracy exp at all. Accuracy gains no exp for AoE attacks.
 Critical Difficulty experience is based on Critical Accuracy if critted.
 Evasion exp is based on Accuracy if hit.
 Heals can now be configured to not validate if the base heal would overrun the target stat. Ability services now honor this as well in determining max required heals from a menu item.


Room Additions and Changes


 Attribute training speed is now based on room level, not a speed stat. This means it starts slow, but as the base improves, attribute training will get faster.
 Training now costs more in general.
 Project professions no longer add difficulty to work cost, but instead have a base work cost. Skill does not reduce cost, so if contributing to a building project costs 5 stamina per turn, you can’t (currently) reduce that.
 Project rooms now provide ambient mana matched to the mana required to level the associated profession path (so civilians earn the mana they need to level while working).
 The cafeteria provides all ambient mana.
 Mana generation for the base only occurs now at the System Pylon and in each Hall of Magic (based on room level).


Path Additions and Changes


 Added Elementalist, Primordialist, and Orthogonalist deep paths. Max levels in these paths can only be unlocked by leveling the standard magic paths. You can’t buy these at the shop (although I won’t rule out lore finds in the wilds unlocking some max levels for these paths).
 Added Archmage deep path. Max levels in this path can only be unlocked by leveling the Elementalist, Primordialist, and Orthogonalist deep paths. All of these paths add a lot more stats than normal paths, and I intend to add powerful synergistic magic abilities to them as well (such as Prismatic abilities for the Archmage).
 Civilian paths now provide magic affinity levels. Civilian paths level up via the magic type linked to the profession speed stat. So, for instance, mushroom harvesting uses Perception as its speed stat, and its path levels up via Dark Mana.


Shop Additions and Changes

 Added death protection for buffs. (Purchased for credits, consumed on death keeping your buffs going.)
 Base-manufactured equipment now costs supply per level on the back end, and all equipment costs extra per level. So a Chainsword 1 might cost 500 prestige and 1 chainsword supply, while a Chainsword 5 might cost 2500 and 5 supply.
 Sold equipment adds to base supply per level of the equipment.
 Equipment item level can now be upgraded at the shop, for both credits (infinite supply) or prestige (limited supply). This costs exactly what it would cost new. Both equipped and inventory items can be upgraded.
 New equipment can be purchased at all levels up to the researched max.
 Max purchases are no longer limited by member count. This means that if members simultaneously buy the same items, item supply could go negative. I’ve decided this is fine; it just means it will take that much longer for the base supply chain to catch up and make that item purchasable for credits again.


Here the base has 5 supply for chainswords, and a level 4 chainsword is selected, making all but a level 1 chainsword out of supply:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/7284caf16151ec8ff08fe596124bab0ffed21286.png

Item Additions and Changes


 Equipment no longer stacks in inventory.


Character Additions and Changes

Improved the AI action system, and implemented it for civilians. They will now do the following in order:


 If hungry, they'll go to the Cafeteria and buy food (either their profession-buff food, or free food if they can’t afford it).
 If their home project room has a project running they can help with, they’ll go work on it.
 If they can buy max levels for their path or targeted development stat exp levels, they'll go to the shop and buy them. They'll also buy mana.
 If they can train any of their development stats, they'll do so.
 If nothing else matches, they’ll hang out at the cafeteria.


Stat Additions and Changes


 Investiture now adds more mana-based stats.
 Civilians and combat units now have different investiture configurations (so that combat units can earn combat path unlocks via investiture).
 Civilians with free stats on level up now add them to the speed attribute for their profession (specifically, they split them between all attributes listed in their targeted development stats).

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Ability Mechanics Additions and Changes


 Added abilities that can remove zone environments.
 Zone environments can now be temporary, losing a level each turn until gone.
 Zones can now apply environments per turn, so while you could temporarily remove levels of a Cold Wind environment, the zone will reapply it.
 Environments can conflict. Depending on the situation, they will either reduce levels of existing environments, or trigger a Distortion Storm, which temporarily increases ambient distortion in the zone. Distortion weakens all magic except Arcane, and boosts Arcane.
 The AoE missile attack now triggers a temporary Inferno environment at the level of the missile attack: anything susceptible takes Burning stacks until the Inferno is spent.
 Rooms handle environment conflicts differently: they simply cancel each other (no distortion storms inside the base).
 Abilities can now query for a particular item proficiency and tag equipped to an equipment slot, and if true, will use any equipment stats defined by the slot. This means that, for instance, I can have basic blade abilities on a sword, but also provide innate abilities that use the sword and its stats, while a knife sidearm won't enable the innate abilities or contribute stats.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Scrapper Base Changes


 The base now has a resource refinery, called the Resource Concentrator, with projects for things like converting rubble into concrete, crystal shards into crystals, and scrap metal into metal bars. Room levels unlock “Concentratologist” NPCs, path levels in the shop, and skill exp in the shop. The room also has a training station for the skill.
 The base now has a Leatherworks, with armor projects, NPCs, path levels, training station, and skill exp shop listings.
 Monster Processing now produces biomass, which can be used by the Kitchens to make ration cubes. Slime monster remains can also be converted into jelly (which will either be used for food, or for a pharmaturgical product).
 Monster Processing also unlocks the Anomalous Nexus, which now has the Nexus Farmer and Nexus Hunter professions, skills, trainers, and NPCs.
 The base Core now provides Builder NPCs, construction path levels and skill exp, and the construction skill training station.
 Existing professional rooms now have a training station for their profession, as well as the associated NPC unlocks, path level unlocks, and skill exp unlocks.
 Rooms and members no longer need slots, since they are unlocked via the room build tree.


Equipment Proficiencies

Equipment items now have associated proficiencies on characters, and require characters to have X levels in the proficiency in order to equip the item. So, scrapper armor might require 5 proficiency in medium armor to equip it.

Any additional proficiency over the requirement can increase beneficial stats from items, and reduce harmful ones, up to double beneficial and half harmful (including encumbrance).

So, having a proficiency of 20 in medium armor would allow equipping Scrapper Armor at proficiency 5, providing 15 extra proficiency to boost resists granted by the armor (and reduce encumbrance). If Scrapper Armor had 25 blunt resist, the effective resist would be 40, and you’d need 30 total proficiency in medium armor to max out the resist at 50.

Since resists (and other stats) continually go up as item level increases, the proficiency required to get the most out of an item will also increase.

These are the equipment proficiencies I've added so far (but I intend to add more):

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/e1576904c5a2d294c731b1003a5dd2a56e816d27.png

Ability Proficiencies

Proficiencies also boost abilities. Right now, the boost can be up to double heal power, buff/debuff power, damage, accuracy, and so forth. This includes all other bonuses to those stats (which might change, depending on balance). Proficiencies can also reduce ability costs up to half (not including ammo).

Innate abilities also have proficiencies. In the case of a weapon ability, the weapon proficiency is used, not the ability proficiency.

So, when casting an innate fireball, fire affinity might be used as the proficiency rating, but if the fireball is being cast from a magic staff, magic staff proficiency would be used instead.

Proficiency Usage Exp

Proficiencies gain usage exp via abilities, whether on offense or defense.

I intend proficiencies to also be trainable at stations in the base, with system exp levels purchasable for credits at the shop (with, as usual, the number of purchases determined by the source room level).

Scrapper Base

The base is now the “Scrapper Base”. “Scrapper” indicates both scavenging and fighting. :)

I want the base to start with a minimal set of self-sustainable rooms that provide the means to fuel expansion, including starter gear and consumables.

With that in mind, this a tentative list of the starter rooms:

 Powertech Factory (makes industrial cutters, chainswords, powered knives, and small batteries)
 Leatherworks (makes scrapper armor out of monster leather and metals, this set is effectively “medium”)
 Kitchens (converts ingredients into food, perhaps starting with turning biomass into the ration cube)
 Refabrication (refines rubble into concrete, scrap metal into metal bars, etc, for use in constructing new rooms, upgrading room levels, or adding item supply)
 Monster Processing (breaks down monster remains into useful parts, like biomass).
 Research Lab (levels starter items supplied by the crafting rooms)
 Residential (allows resting for health/stamina recovery, improved per level; also adds max member count, but that may change)
 Core (now increases max room level cap)


Room Unlocks

Room levels can now unlock new rooms. For instance, getting Residential to level 5 might unlock the Medbay, and Medbay 5 might unlock the Pharmaturgium, and Pharmaturgium 5 might unlock the Myceliary.

Since this web of unlocks effectively allows base-building decisions via the upgrades that are chosen and pushed, I’m thinking of removing the empty room slot requirement. I’m also thinking that some rooms, like those for refining, crafting, or growing, could be unlocked multiple times.

I also intend to make unlocking the rooms that provide things like magic weapons and paths, for instance, to be a bit more difficult (and rewarding). :)

Character Unlocks

Room levels can now unlock new characters in the hiring system. A Barracks room, for instance, might unlock a Soldier every 5th level, or the Medbay might unlock a Medic every 10th level.

Like room slots, I’m thinking of removing max member slots in favor of this system. The unlocked characters would still need to be hired.

I’m also considering allowing the level of hirable characters to be increased.

Project and Shop Unlocks

Project rooms can unlock purchases in the shop for the profession associated with their type of project. So, Hydroponics room levels might add shop listings for Harvester path max levels.

Research projects can unlock crafting supply projects and shop listings for new items. Further research levels increase the level of items purchased.

A "Shotguns" research project, for instance, might unlock the Shotgun 1 and Shotgun Ammo item sell listings in the shop, and their associated crafting supply projects in the Firearms Factory crafting room. Shotguns 2 research would in turn increase the level of the purchasable item to 2.

Teleporter System

The base now connects to the world of the current scenario via a teleportation network accessible from the base core. At scenario start, a single remote teleporter is created in a designated world zone. Further teleporters can be created by conquering enemy rifts.

Monsters can attack teleporters, and if all teleporters in the world are destroyed, the scenario is lost. Teleporters can be repaired, including destroyed teleporters (although you’ll need to get there the long way).

I’m thinking I want research to improve teleporter defenses, and possibly give them turret-like abilities, but we’ll see.

Note that monsters can’t convert destroyed teleporters back into spawners.

Other Changes

 The System premium currency is now called credits (as opposed to the Scrapper Base currency, which is still called prestige).
 Shop item listings are now split into ammo, consumables, and equipment.
 Any standard item supplied by a crafting room is duplicated as a System item offered for credits. System items get their own categories in the shop. (Base-produced items are bought for prestige.)
 Unlimited mana is now sold for credits.
 Earned prestige from either item sales or currency exchange can now be used immediately in the shop.
 Item sale price is now determined by both item value and the currency exchange rate. The credits price is item value, and the prestige price is item value times the exchange rate. Note that the exchange rate doesn’t change, and neither do prices (you can’t game the shop: if you buy an item for credits, and sell for prestige, it’s the same as buying prestige with credits). Item level doesn't currently affect price.
 When a project is started, if it’s priority was at zero, it’s moved to the back of the list. Projects that are instantly completed via credits are also moved to the back.

New Room Construction

The base has room slots that can be populated by new rooms, and it unlocks new room slots as it levels. When a room type is unlocked, it’s added at the bottom of the construction priority list.

If a room slot is available, and the base can afford the construction cost, the room is created at level 0, with a level 1 upgrade project populated. Once the level 1 upgrade is complete, the room’s basic functions are enabled.

Note that there can only be one room per type.

I intend the base to start with a few rooms (possibly just the base core, we’ll see), and provide the player with the opportunity to influence base build order.

Parallel Room Upgrades

Instead of being limited to one or two simultaneous room upgrades, construction can be now parallel on all rooms. 

Note that upgrades-in-progress don't disable the primary function of the room.

Room Upgrade Costs

These can now change per level, not just in quantity, but in type. I’m thinking later levels will require more complex resources.

Max Base Members

This is now determined largely by the level of the Residential room (though the base core will probably provide a small amount).

Harvest Projects

Each harvest node in a grow room (such as Hydroponics) populates a project after X turns. When the harvest project is complete, the harvest population timer restarts. Room level reduces the turns required to populate a harvest.

Room Action Presentation

All room actions now display under objects spotted within the zone, with their own names and descriptions. The base shop, for instance, can now be found under the System Pylon, as can the leveling dialog. (This makes the base consistent with how actions are presented in the world.)

Also, zones now have a ground target where the searching action can be found (if applicable). AoE abilities can also be targeted on ground, even if no targets are spotted.

Item Shop

The existence and level of items in the shop are now handled by events like research or faction level. So, if you wanted higher level heavy armor in the shop, you might advance the heavy armor research. :)

[olist]

 The System can offer infinite supply for premium currency (as opposed to standard base currency). This allows characters to get gear as needed, even if the base is behind on providing supply.

Frost Slimes

I started populating the frost slime monster horde, which required adding new abilities and conditions, and that led into many updates on abilities and conditions. :)

All slimes get the abilities Pseudopod Spike and Frost Touch. The spike is a stamina-based physical ability, while frost touch requires ambient water mana.

All slimes (so far) will be able to plant and tend their monster growths that increase ambient water mana.

Damage Reflection

I re-implemented damage reflection. Reflection is based on damage type, and simply requires a successful enemy hit of its damage type, and does true damage to the enemy, bypassing resists.

I think that might be an interesting build choice: to focus on stacking reflects and armor for various kinds of damage, while making yourself as easy as possible to hit. :)

Note that reflect doesn’t mitigate incoming damage. Also, it gains exp based on amount of reflect.

Other Damage Changes


 I also re-implemented lifesteal. Lifesteal requires direct damage of its type, and can be no more than damage done, or the starting health of the target. Lifesteal gains exp based on health stolen (even if not needed).
 The evasion mechanic is now merged with the hit difficulty mechanic. Hit difficulty and crit difficulty experience can be gained on successful enemy hits that aren’t AoE or blindsides.
 Physical damage now has blunt, pierce, and slash variants. 
 Added falloff for accuracy, steal, and armor piercing (for abilities with repetitions like a machine gun burst).
 Repetition and cooldowns are now levelable stats (leveling an ability might increase repetitions, and decrease cooldowns).
 Can do massive crits (triple damage) versus normal crits (double damage). Massive crits are either from blindsides, or direct attacks in which accuracy is more than double critical defense.
 Can now get exp for character stats that boost conditions, armor-piercing, ability power, and resists to negative conditions.

Ability Classes

Abilities now have a power source class and a target effect/resist class. Resist classes can either be resistance to hostile effects, or resistance to beneficial effects. 

Piercing damage, for instance, could be done by an Icicle ability powered by water magic, an Earth Bullet ability powered by earth magic, a Stab ability powered by physical stats, or a Rifle Shot ability powered by technology.

Each power source determines the powerups applied to the ability (Icicle might gain power from ambient water magic, and Stab might gain power from the Strength attribute), as well as what stats gain experience (Icicle might increase water affinity experience, while Stab might increase strength experience).

Resist classes determine experience and powerups for stats like resistance, armor-piercing, accuracy, and lifesteal.

I also added condition classes, that define much the same things for conditions, and I added new conditions like Frostbite, Wounded, and Stunned.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/19e99f19b0a8f9cc48d25fdc9ec2b090c9db028b.png

Other Ability Changes

Toggles can now allow other abilities to skip costs, and block use of abilities. For instance, I added an Industrial Cutter item. Its innate abilities can’t be used unless it’s powered on via a powered cutter toggle, and then it both boosts scavenging skill and provides a Powered Slice ability, whose cost is covered by the toggle.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/dc23d973b4743451979f41541562f91eb1fd64b1.png

The cutter is Noisy, which blocks and cancels stealth abilities.

I added a Chainsword item that does the same thing, except it does more damage, and doesn’t boost scavenging so much. I also added a Jetpack item that allows for noisy flight (no stealth). :)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/4a041a19e52e6306c44793628adc6d945136149c.png

Leveling Requirements

Monster experience leveling requirements are now set by leveling, and can be customized per monster type.

User (and player)-based path leveling now works the same way. Mana requirements are set by the level of the mana investiture, and can vary.

This means costs are no longer set by a formula that directly uses level. Instead, levels 1- 10 might cost an added 50 per level, while 11 - 20, might cost an added 100, but only for water mana: air mana could be cheaper, or have a different profile.

Resource Priorities

The base priority system will no longer tend to the average by auto-increasing priority on projects that weren’t selected. I think this will make for a more interesting overall experience, while making priority shop purchases weightier.

Details:


 Projects have hard-set priority max of 10;
 On successful project start, priority goes down one (except for hiring, which sets to 0);
 Max priority sets eligibility for instant completion (except for hiring and overall resource priority);
 If instant completion is successful, priority resets to 0.


Output Changes

I added an action right-click dialog, with information on requirement checks (you can see that in a previous screenshot). I also added info on experience levels and other components for the stat dialog.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Demo Update

The Pits has icy terrain at its base, while the Refinery is mostly ruins terrain, and shadowed. Rails is mostly wilderness terrain, and cold. I definitely want some frost-slinging slimes and stealthy rats. :)

Details:

 Added ice and wilderness terrain;
 Added locked metal doors to make a hidden zone in the Refinery;
 Added pile of ore blocking access in Refinery;
 Populated zone conceal/cover/ambience stats;
 Added a cold wind environment inflicting a cold condition (drains stamina);
 Added a test armor that provides enough water resistance to stop the player form catching the cold condition from cold winds;
 Added a freezing environment that inflicts frostbite (DoT) and a stronger cold condition (same effect, but requires more resist to block);
 Added a camouflage stat (for now, only affects stealth);
 Added a shadowed environment that provides a buff that increases camouflage.

Forced Cancellation of Ability Toggles

This mechanic allows hostile damage, debuff, or buff actions to also cancel toggled abilities if the action is successful. This works on tags, so if you have a toggled ability with the stealth tag, an illuminate ability might cancel the stealth ability, if it defeats your light resist.

This also applies to actions the character takes: a rifle shot will cancel stealth abilities.

Stealth Update

I moved the stealth ability from being a special case to being a toggled ability (like force field), and the stealth state is now a boolean on/off stat determined by conditions.

In short, this means the player can start multiple kinds of toggled stealth abilities that stack. For example:

 Stamina-based sneaking (stamina cost per turn)
 Ambience-based hiding (no cost per turn, but requires ambient dark mana: auto-cancels if you move out of a zone with dark mana)
 Device-based cloaking (costs power per turn)

Canceling one of them won’t break your stealth (the bool stat returns true as long as it’s greater than 1), though your stealth rating will go down.

This change also means that the stealth rating updates per zone, depending on zone stats, and you get ability exp per turn.

Ability EXP Gain Update

Ability exp gain for usage can now leverage specific results. For instance, accuracy exp only comes from enemy hit or crit difficulty causing misses. Damage exp comes from doing damage, attack speed exp comes from having attacks evaded, and pierce exp comes from defense that wasn’t pierced.

Exp gain also works on defense now, so, for instance, resist exp comes from damage that wasn’t blocked.

Also added some more logic so that attacking objects that can’t evade, or can’t be blindsided, don’t show those stats in the output.

Note that exp gain only affects character stats leveraged by the abilities (like the strength attribute for a melee attack); the abilities themselves don’t currently gain exp.

Cost and EXP Gains for Actions

This affects non-ability-based actions, like:

 Movement
 Searching
 Scavenging
 Studying
 Repairing
 Planting (only for monsters right now)
 Growing (only for monsters right now)
 Lockpicking

Basic formula I’m testing:

 To do the action, your skill must at least be equal to difficulty;
 Difficulty is added to action cost;
 Any skill remainder from the difficulty check is removed from cost;
 If the action is progress-based (all but movement so far), progress equals your relevant speed stat plus any skill remainder from the cost check;
 Exp can equal cost (for non-progress actions like transit) or progress (for most professions)
 Faction payment for progress-based actions is the progress gained;
 If an ability is used to bypass the progress requirement to complete the action, exp is only gained for the ability.

Vars can be modded by the zone itself, by zone objects, and by the relevant profession. The types of stats involved are configured primarily by the professions involved (but also terrain).

The planting action, for instance, is defined by the terrain, so different types of terrains will be more conducive to various kinds of monster growths.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Ability Toggles

I added abilities that once enabled, re-run automatically per turn, re-applying cost checks and any effects. The player can disable them at any time, canceling the costs and effects.

Costs can include ambient mana levels, so you might have an ability that will run as long as there’s 5 ambient fire mana. Or, it might be based on stored mana, or stamina, or ammo, or something else. If any requirements are not met, the ability auto-cancels.

If a toggled ability is from equipment, the ability will cancel if the item is unequipped.

These abilities require either self or area targeting. I intend to allow damaging auras to be toggled this way, but it can also include health regen, stat buffs, etc.

Power System

Characters can now have a power bar, like stamina or health, to run mundane equipment like force field generators or energy weapons.

Power is currently rechargeable at the base core (free but slow) or with consumables like batteries. Power is also zeroed at death if the user hasn't purchased death protection.

Force Field

I reworked the force field mechanic to exploit ability toggles and power to continually apply a force field buff to the player, as long as the player can afford the power cost. This buff currently increases a defense rating.

I’d like to have multiple items that provide different kinds of powered fields, to, say, increase physical resists, or elemental resists, or primordial resists, or evasion, or health regen, and so forth.

I also want to have fields that use ambient mana, not power (or perhaps both, for more powerful fields).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/4e0fe9b12504dbed8e69ab7263fbc439393a667a.png

Max Shop Purchases

Max purchases allowed of paths, abilities, perks, and stat exp in the shop is no longer defined directly by base level. It can be changed by base levels, but also by completed research, or lore discoveries in the world.

So, for example, an earth magic research might add more max path levels for “path of earth magic”. Or, you might uncover hidden lore in a locked room somewhere, that adds a few levels of rare paths or abilities to the shop. :)

Lore and Research 

Lore objects can now unlock new research, or add progress to existing research. So, say, studying a strange object in the wilds might boost energy weapons research. :)

Notes on research:

 Excess progress is now applied to next level (allowing multiple research levels at once, if there’s enough).
 Research no longer applies to room max level. I decided that requiring research and upgrade costs to level a room was a double-bottleneck, that would be more frustrating than fun.
 Research length now increases with level. I’d like to adjust this to be modifiable by more than level.
 Research priorities are color-coded to show what is currently researchable (based on lab level). I’m considering, however, whether lab level should just be a research speed boost, and not a gate.

NPCs, Traits, and Behaviors

I’ve decided that NPC behaviors will be customized to their classes. So, a Fire Engineer will always make the same decisions as other Fire Engineers, though they will diverge from Water Engineers.

In short, I want an experienced player to see the character class name and have a good idea of its behaviors without having to click through dialogs to see a trait-set.

It’s still possible for NPCs to change what decisions they can make as they level (so a Fire Engineer that had more access to dark mana than fire mana might have different ability unlocks than one with access to more fire mana).

Demo Scenario

The setting for the main campaign is a world once dominated by a magitech civilization codenamed Dystopia, but destroyed by monsters. The demo starts in a post-apocalyptic Dystopian mining complex in a low-magic sector far in the north of the world.

The complex currently has three major areas: the Pits, a massive, strip-mined, artificial crater with a frozen lake at the bottom; the Refinery, a megastructure where metal was smelted out of ore; and the Rails, which connected the two and now hosts decaying mining machinery and wrecked trains.

I intend the Pits to have a Slime rift, while the Refinery will have a Rat rift. They’ll be fighting each other for territory, mostly in the Rails. The System scavenger base will also connect to the Rails. The objectives will be something like scavenge X resources, get the base to Y level, and close one of the rifts (we’ll see).

Right now, I have about twenty zones I’m building to fill out those areas. I’d like a hidden zone or two, with a nice reward in them, visible obstacles you can either destroy or go around, as well as zones where you might want to clear out some debris to lower terrain difficulty, so you can search the zone better.

More:

 I added logical areas that are collections of zones, simply for text and descriptions.
 Moving to a new zone displays a short description in the player log.
 Moving to a new zone will auto-select a target other than the opening the player just used (if possible).

Saving is instant; currently, there are no savegame overwrites. Each save button is only active if the current turn isn't saved. There’s a save button in main, and one in world.

I also added an autosave system, that can be disabled, or configured to save periodically, with options from every turn to every 100th turn.

Attribute Leveling System

Attributes now use the standard leveling system, which means they can easily be configured with the following:

 Bonus stats at X level

I might even wire in other things like ability level awards. I’m also considering migrating magic affinities to work the same way.

Note that the bonus stats can't be other attributes (to prevent looping). Also, stat bonuses from attribute levels can be temporarily reduced by debuffs.

Equipment Weight System

Equipment now has a weight stat, and system users now have burden and max burden stats. The player can't equip items with weight past max burden.

 The burden and max burden stats can be affected by buffs and debuffs.
 The max burden stat can also be affected by attributes like strength.
 Item weight can be affected by item levels.

I’d like to add encumbered and immobilized states.

Base Hiring System

The base can now hire new members. It has a max member stat, which can be affected by leveling. Hiring costs system resources (though it could cost mana too), and new members will show up the next turn.

The list of possible hires can be added to or improved by faction levels or research. Hiring doesn't remove the option from the list, though it adjusts hiring priority (any class of NPC not hired gains priority for the next hire).

The player can spend prestige to change hiring priority in the shop, and the player can also adjust high-level resource priority (for instance, will hiring be considered before construction).

Note that currently members can't be lost; if killed, they will respawn (losing mana and gear like the player).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/b1ac6b895eec52831078e5a56c6965bd288d18eb.png

Auto-choice Leveling System

NPCs can now exploit choices from leveling. The decisions are currently basic: free stats are allocated to the first lowest attribute, and all other choices will be the first in the list.

While I’m hoping to develop that to be more interesting, the primary benefit for now is that NPCs and the player can use the same paths.

notes.notes:
Game Introduction

This uses a conversation with the System to introduces the game’s premise and basic elements. It’s skippable, so you can get straight to character creation.

I want to make the information available in-game as well, but we’ll see.

Character Creation

This allows you to select a starting path, a starting mana investiture into that path, and a starting profession. These choices aren’t exclusive; you’ll later be able to unlock and progress all of them.

Note that I didn’t want character creation to present you with an overwhelming number of choices, for which a new player would have no context. I also didn’t want a rigid class system; I’d rather allow opportunity cost to determine limits: you won’t be able to max everything, but you should also be able to find many effective combinations (including those I didn’t think of).

I may add other choices, such as starter gear.

Here you can see what the current character creation framework looks like:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/9941c908b76f5a72f0eb668f0314d3ee89a959ee.png

Scenario System

The game is now a series of scenarios in a campaign. Completing a scenario detaches the System scavenger base from the current world sector, and attaches it to another, while preserving all base and member progression (including the player’s).

The process relocates any base members not on base back to the core room, and evicts any monsters on base. The spatial jump takes one turn, and disorients all base members (including the player). You get a dialog showing stats from the completed scenario, and information on the next. Finishing the campaign also provides a final stat sheet.

I want to construct a balanced progression of scenarios, from easy to near-impossible, and if I have a permanent demo, it will likely be the first scenario. I’m also considering whether or not to have a high-score list in the main menu, but at a minimum, I want the game to autosave a victory so you can always re-load it and look at the stats.

Ideally, I’d have scenario choices and branching paths, but that’s probably too much. Each scenario will be a hand-built, customized world, with its own biomes, themes, and monsters, and we’ll see how many of those I can make. :)

Another possibility I’m considering is allowing the base members to influence in some way when to leave (such as a vote), so that scenario completion isn’t sudden, and allows you to continue to exploit a scenario’s resources before heading on, but we’ll see. I’d want some kind of downside to that (future scenarios get harder, for instance, or your reward for scenario completion will be lessened).

Victory Conditions

To complete a scenario, the base must collectively complete various quests. These can range from conquering X spawners, acquiring X number of Y resource, and so forth. I’d also like to add optional quests, with quest rewards. (Again, these would be collective, not individual.)

Quest progress is displayed in a quest log.

The current loss condition is the destruction of the System Pylon turret in the base core. This ends the scenario, but not the campaign (unless it’s the last scenario). I’m considering, however, whether it should be a complete loss.

Since the player and all NPCs can teleport straight to the pylon from nearly anywhere, and the turret itself is a powerful weapon, it shouldn’t be easy to lose.

World Interface Layout

Base projects and current quests are now on the left panel, and the incoming log, zone log, base log, and world log are on the right panel. The targeting panel layout should be improved, including warnings for being attacked and being damaged.

Interface Improvements

Obstacles in openings are also displayed here, with access status and information on whether you can spot through the obstacle to the other side of the opening.

Possible actions on target are then listed, including actions that failed because you lack a requirement (such as a high-enough stat).
