notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Action-based Stealth System

Characters can now enter stealth via an action. Some actions (like firing a rifle) break stealth, while others (like using a knife) don’t. Stealth can also be broken if an enemy directly targets the character.

Entering stealth gens a value which is then dynamically combined per turn with zone stats (such as concealment) to determine a final rating per turn. If an enemy detection rating defeats stealth, then that enemy can spot and target you. (Note that defeating stealth is twice as hard at range.)

Attacking while stealthed against an enemy that cannot see you applies an automatic blindside crit that can’t be evaded. (This also applies to attacks that break stealth.)

Rubble System and Corpse Decay

Damaging or destroying objects in the world can now create new “rubble” objects. Damaging a tank wreck, for instance, might start a scrap metal pile.

Rubble objects level with added hit points (and can thus add more stats to zone, like concealment or terrain difficulty), and lose levels with lost HP. This leveling system also applies to monstrous growths.

Corpses now decay over time, and can create their own “rubble” objects (like a corpse pile, or bone pile). Inventory can be transferred from the decayed corpse to the pile, allowing the pile to be looted. (This also works on zone objects.) Mana in the corpse is currently lost.

I’d like to add flags to items such that some might be destroyed on a decay/destroy transfer to a pile. Note that destroying a scavengeable object does not transfer any hidden items it might have contained (so spamming AoE can destroy unique items in the zone).

New Rooms at Base


 Medbay (healing for a price)
 Primordial Orrery (life/death/light/dark mana)
 Residential (free health/stamina via resting)
 Simulators (training)


The Medbay provides healing, debuff removal, and buffs.  As it levels, the services will get more powerful (and possibly less expensive), and new services may be added. Note that heals or removals may be stacked to do a full heal or removal in one go.

The Primordial Orrery is the life/death/light/dark counterpart to the Elemental Refractory. Both now provide training in their respective resists and affinities. Resistance training now costs hit points (and prestige). Note that arcane resist and affinity is trained at the System Pylon.

The Residential level provides a rest option for free health and stamina recovery (though slower than the medbay). Leveling will increase how much you gain by resting. I also want to add item and mana storage, possibly equipment set management, and maybe even things like trophies (but we’ll see).

The Simulators level currently provides training for attributes and physical resists, and I may expand that to include other stats.

Note that training can now cost prestige, mana, stamina, hit points and so forth.

Other Changes


 Abilities can now use zone stats to increase power and face added resists. So a death ability might face added resistance if used in a life-ambient zone, but gain power if used in a death-ambient zone. If ranged, this applies to both from source and destination zones, so ambient mana levels in both zones should become more interesting.
 Added a distortion stat to zones, which I can leverage to make magic abilities harder to use. (I’m thinking arcane abilities will ignore distortion, and possibly even benefit from it.)
 Conditions can now be persistent (like diseases).
 Conditions can now include zone stats on their effect (note that zones can also affect condition power via abilities).
 Environment-applied conditions from zones can now affect zone objects.
 Room upgrades no longer require capacity stats from faction: just research. I figured that the capacity mechanic, while standard for 4X games, forced certain rooms to be upgraded first, which removed interesting choices. (If this doesn't play well, however, I can re-add capacity requirements.)
 Fuel for regen only burns per tick, not via tick magnitude (so increasing health regen will always be desirable and use calories efficiently).
 The player now has a wait action.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Combat Abilities

Combat consists of abilities applied to targets. There are six types of abilities:


 Damage
 Heal
 Buff
 Debuff
 Buff removal
 Debuff removal


Damage and heal abilities currently affect hit points only, but can apply on-success conditions to affect other stats. Damage and heals can fail to have any effect if target resistance is too high.

Buffs and debuffs can apply conditions on success, if they overcome resistance. (Buffs and heals may be hampered by toxicity or magical anti-healing.)

Removal abilities can eliminate conditions on success, but must overcome target condition power.

Notes:


 All abilities can be area-of-effect. AoE abilities do double power to target, and normal power to everything else.
 Abilities have innate stats that level up as abilities do, but equipment abilities can also gain boosts from their source equipment, and all abilities can gain boosts from character stats.
 Abilities can provide usage experience to character stats. Exp gain can be static (X per use), or dynamic based on performance of the ability. In that case, failure provides the most experience. For instance, damage reduction from enemy resistance is added to exp. Attacking powerful enemies can thus provide a lot of exp (even if no damage is done).


Status Conditions

There are four types of status conditions:


 Damage over time
 Heal over time
 Buff stats
 Debuff stats


Damage over time conditions ignore resists (they do true damage). Heal over time also ignores any applicable resists. Buff or debuff conditions can affect multiple stats, with the same magnitude.

Notes:

 Conditions have a power rating, which must be overcome in order to be directly removed. The power rating does not affect the magnitude of the condition, however.
 Conditions applied on-success from damage or heal abilities use the damage or heal magnitude as their power. So, bleeding from a 1-damage hit will be much easier to remove than bleeding from a 100-damage hit.
 Removal attempts are cumulative: five 20-power remove bleeding attempts will clear a 100-power bleed.
 Condition adds are procced before removes.
 Conditions also have stacks, max stacks, duration, max duration, and stack accrual stats.
 Conditions do not provide experience, only abilities do.


Evasion Changes

Evasion now applies both to melee and ranged attacks (alteration has been removed). Successful evasion costs stamina, the cost defined per character (I anticipate that smaller enemies will have less cost to evade).

Currently, it works like this:

[olist]
 On the defender, hit difficulty is added to critical difficulty. If the attack is ranged, concealment is added to critical difficulty. (I may add cover as well, and tweak further if the ranged attack is in the same zone or not.)
 If attacker accuracy is greater than double critical difficulty, it’s a guaranteed crit.
 If accuracy is greater than critical difficulty, evasion is checked for both crit and hit.
 If evasion is at least equal to attack speed, the crit is avoided for a stamina cost.
 If evasion is at least equal to double attack speed, the hit is avoided for an additional stamina cost.
 If accuracy is greater than hit difficulty, evasion is checked for hit.
 If evasion is at least equal to attack speed, the hit is avoided for a stamina cost.
[/olist]

Notes:


 If any avoidance occurs, the attacker gains extra experience. So, missing outright provides the most exp.
 Total evasion is divided among all incoming attacks. So, a character with 100 evasion facing 10 simultaneous attacks can only apply 10 evasion to each attack stack.
 Evasion is not procced if no damage would be done.
Currently, a crit is double damage (after damage reduction).

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Lore Objects and Items

Lore objects are anything providing a study task to users: things like graffiti, posters, or arcane machinery.

A studying task uses a lore skill for a gate and an attribute for speed, and when complete provides a reward, such as lore exp in a stat, applied to all members of the faction (as well as a flavor text to tell a story).

Study actions can only be completed once.

Lore items are consumables like journals that provide a one-time exp boost, potentially to all faction members. 

Stats and Experience

Stats can now gain levels from the following five types of experience:


 Alchemical
 Lore
 System
 Training
 Usage


Levels from these experience types are tracked separately, and do not conflict or affect each other. Levels from free stats, or perks, or any other kind of leveling also do not interfere with these levels.

Alchemical levels will likely come from potions concocted in the Pharmaturgium from monstrous growths. Unlike lore consumables, alchemical exp consumables would only affect the consuming user.

System levels can come from the shop, and I'm hoping from quests (but we'll see). Training comes from stations within the base, and usage can happen whenever a stat is used.

Leveling Changes


 Path awards now provide max levels, not simply an unlock, so the same path can be awarded multiple times, allowing the player to invest more mana in it, and possibly get more unlocks from the path;
 Perks now use the leveling system, so they can provide more flexible bonuses;
 Multiple ability levels, path max levels, and perk levels can be provided in a single award;
 Path, ability, stat, and perk awards can now be every X level, starting at Y level, and ending at Z level.


Shop Changes


 All ability, perk, and path purchases are limited in count to faction level, and this is tracked per member;
 System experience in stats can be purchased, with the above limitation;
 New stat, ability, path, and perk listings can be unlocked by research or faction levels;
 Users can sell non-leveled items to faction, based on an innate value.


Mana Investiture Levels

For system users, the total mana levels invested across all paths are now tracked. Focusing on leveling paths with fire mana, for instance, would result in a high level of fire mana investiture.

Leveling up investiture provides rewards which could include things like resists and affinities, as well as potentially perks, abilities, and paths.

Other Changes


 Doors can now be locked and scavenged like other objects;
 Objects can either have all-or-nothing HP (like doors), or instead use a level-reduction mechanic (like scavengable piles of rubble);
 Spawners have a max they can spawn of any monster type; leveling the spawner can increase this max;
 Monsters can now restore their growths if damaged;
 Users destroying a scavengable object now gather its base award to faction.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Objects in Zones

Zone objects, such as gather nodes, can now change the stats of the zone, affecting things like ambient mana, cover, and terrain difficulty. Objects can have levels, each level increasing their effect on the zone.

Gathering or scavenging these objects reduces their levels, reducing their effect on the zone.

Monstrous Growths

Monsters can now plant, build, and level constructs and growths to increase the ambient mana they need. In turn, they will attack growths from other monsters. The player and other users can destroy or gather these growths for resources.

If a monster spawner is conquered by the player, a resource associated with the monster horde will be available to farm in the Anomalous Nexus.

Destructible Objects

Not only are monster growths destructible, but many other objects will be (including types of gather nodes). AoE can damage or inflict status conditions like burning on objects in zones.

Lootable Objects

While gather nodes can provide extra items when gathered, some objects can be looted outright for items (and then scavenged for more loot).

Lootable objects can also be locked, requiring the appropriate skill to advance a task for breaking the lock, or they can be broken outright if you have an ability such as Fire Touch at a high enough level.
 
There can be multiple kinds of locks and skills required to unlock them. I intend to apply this functionality to doors and windows as well.

Terrain Gating

To enter a zone, you need the associated terrain skill equal or greater to terrain difficulty. To search a zone for hidden objects or openings, you need terrain skill that equals the difficulty times the level of the search.

So, a ten difficulty urban terrain would require twenty urban terrain skill for a level two search. Scavenging and removing objects to lower terrain difficulty can make that easier (and also make it easier for monsters to enter the zone).

The hidden objects in the zone determine the max search level. A level three hidden object requires level three search completion to reveal.

Speed Mechanics

With all the X of Y progress tasks in the game, I decided that your base attributes, not special speed stats, will be used as much as possible to determine the speed of progress-advancing actions.

So, the speed of picking a lock would be determined by your dexterity score, the speed of hacking a lock would be determined by your intelligence score, and the speed of searching an urban zone would be determined by your perception score.

Note that you gain a small amount of experience in an attribute when leveraging it for speed.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
System Base Mana Economy

Each room in the System base (not counting the surface gate) both generates mana to the faction, and provides a small amount of ambient mana that users can absorb. The faction, in turn, offers mana for sale (for prestige) at the shop.

Rooms generate mana types consistent with their purpose. For instance, I added a new mushroom-harvesting room called a Myceliary, that provides dark mana.

I also consolidated the Waterworks and Mana Reactor into the Elemental Refractory. This room has no tasks (right now), but provides the most total ambient mana (all four elemental types). This room also provides things like power and water capacity that other rooms need to be upgraded.

The current mana direction of each room:


Base core (System pylon) - arcane
Fabrication - earth and fire
Hydroponics - life (and probably water)
Monster Processing - death
Anomalous Nexus - arcane
Kitchens - air and fire
Pharmaturgium - life and death
Elemental Refractory - fire, air, earth, water
Myceliary - dark
Terrarium - earth (and probably life)
Research Lab - light


Spawner Destruction Mechanics

Spawners are a form of rift or spatial anomaly that can spawn monsters, level up, and provide bonuses to its spawns. Each spawner belongs to a greater entity called a horde (the monster counter to the System base faction).

Both System users and monsters can conquer spawners and subvert the anomaly. When users do so, the System base gains a teleport in that zone (that cannot be conquered), and also gains levels in farming the horde to which the spawner belongs.

Hordes both gain levels when their spawners level, and also by conquering other spawners (they gain the level of the conquered spawner). Once they conquer a spawner, hordes can then start spawning their own monsters there (though right now they need to re-level the spawner).

Note that spawners have a permanent spatial distortion effect that blocks the teleport home action of System users.

Monster farming

When the System base conquers spawners, it’s considered signature acquisition to the home plane of the owning hordes. The Anomalous Nexus room at the base will then allow monsters from that horde to be farmed, earning corpses for Monster Processing.

As more spawners are conquered, the base gains levels in farming those hordes, which can unlock new options.

In practice, as the player progresses through the scenarios, the Nexus will allow ready access to monstrous resources that may not exist in the current scenario, thus allowing certain items to continue to be crafted.

Abilities and Ambient Mana

To prepare for how monsters fight, abilities can now have an ambient mana requirement. My plan is that monsters will use external magic, meaning they don’t collect mana to use as fuel for abilities, but rather leverage the ambient mana.

If a zone has five ambient dark mana, a Giant Rat could use an ability requiring three ambient dark mana indefinitely, but not one requiring ten. So, powerful abilities will require high ambience, and powerful monsters will thus tend to avoid low ambience, where their capabilities will be diminished.

Ambient mana will thus tend to define the borders of monster territory, as well as signal more dangerous areas.

Note that to help configure more interesting monster combat orders, I also added the option of cooldowns to abilities.

External Magic and User Build Paths

I intend to give System users the option of following external magic paths as well as internal. In broad strokes, the upside of external magic is that it doesn’t spend absorbed mana like internal, thus allowing all absorbed mana to be spent on path upgrades.

The downside is that the magic available will be limited, and in many cases what’s available will be targeting the strength of the enemy. Using dark mana abilities against a monster that likes dark mana should be difficult.

Internal magic, of course, spends mana, but can be used anywhere, making it easier to bring to bear abilities that target enemy weaknesses.

Mundane weapons can also be used anywhere, and don’t spend mana. They, however, will either have an ammo requirement, be a melee weapon with a stamina requirement, or be a consumable (like a grenade). They’ll also tend to do physical damage types only.

Weapons could also use internal or external magic, but I’d consider them as options within those build paths.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Looting

Looting involves monsters looting monsters or system users, users looting the same, and tiebreaking.

When monsters loot corpses, they gain exp based on the level of the corpse, and the corpse is destroyed. Items are destroyed (although I may change that). Ties between monsters currently make no difference to outcome.

When users loot monsters, both the faction base and the users gain system currency (called sysres). The base also gains a corpse, and the users can gain mana, depending on the mana type of the monster and the users’ mana affinity.

When a user loots the corpse of a user, the contents of the corpse are salvaged to the owner of the corpse. Ties between users make no difference.

Ties between monsters and users are broken by total levels: whichever side has the most gets the loot. If levels are equal, each side gets something, but as not as much as they would have otherwise.

Monster Processing

The base has a new monster processing room with projects to turn monster corpses into useful crafting materials. The higher the level the project, the more items can be extracted from each corpse, and the more corpses can be processed per project run.

Since the idea is to exterminate monster spawners, I intend that defeating the primary spawner of a monster will unlock a farming option at the base for that kind of monster (say, an abstracted teleport to the home plane of that monster), that way the source of the materials doesn’t vanish.

Note that corpses and extracted materials don’t have levels; only finished items have those. 

System Currency

System currency, or sysres, is the game’s “premium” currency. Faction users can use it to buy one-time death protection for items or mana, exchange it for prestige, and possibly buy other useful things with it (like skill levels).

The base can use sysres to instantly complete high-priority projects that don’t have enough resources to start otherwise.

Another possible use is storage overrun compensation. If there’s one item for sale in the shop, and two users buy it on the same turn, a duplicate is deliberately genned so that both users get what they bought without needing to do a tiebreaker. 

If that mechanic looks too unbalancing, I might charge the base sysres each time.

Base Elevator System

The base core room, which has the System Pylon, now has an elevator nexus to all the internal rooms of the base. The navigation dialog also shows what actions you can do in each room, so you don’t have to pop in and out of each room to check.

That should make moving around the base easier for the player and the NPCs.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/ad4b9de8b13ee99bf22269e35e9250e6c5b185d6.png

Surface Access

The System base is underground, and the core room now has a tunnel to a heavily-defended surface gate room. It has a recessed blast door and two LMG turrets, allowing them and any defenders to used ranged attacks on the surface zone outside the gate.

The core room also has a blast door, and the System Pylon itself is now a powerful AoE turret (that ignores friendlies).

Planned Scenario System

I’m planning to make the game a series of scenarios, in which the System base connects to a sector so that resources can be gathered and monsters killed to improve the base and its users.

For now, I’m thinking that if the monsters make it to the core room, and do enough damage to the Pylon, the base will prematurely disengage from that sector and engage the next.

This should allow me to do diverse scenarios, without trying to fit them all into one simultaneous world. I’d like to allow the base to choose the next scenario, but that means creating more scenarios, so for now, I’m shooting for a simple series (easy to hard).

Ideally, the demo will be the first scenario. :)

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Faction Levels

The player faction now has an overall level, which is the total of all room levels. Each level can provide stats to the faction and stats to all members of the faction (including the player).

Faction level also determines purchase limit for certain things in the shop, like skill levels (so as the faction levels, you can buy more skill levels).

I want to add more to faction levels, including shop unlocks like abilities and paths or new research and project lines.

Structures

All obstacles within openings (doors, windows, and walls) are now separate structures that are treated like characters in the area, so they can, for instance, be attacked. I also added turrets, which are static combat emplacements.

Both structures and rooms are now repairable. Repairing faction structures provides prestige.

Training

Rooms can now provide training actions for skills and stats. Training uses another stat to determine learning speed. So, training a research skill might use intelligence as the learning speed. Training is free, but is capped by room level.

I’d like to add rooms dedicated to training stats, while other rooms might include training among their other functions. I might even add training that costs hit points, like fire resistance training. :)

Note that training levels don't interfere with other kinds of levels, like shop levels, or usage exp levels, or path levels, or perks. All level caps apply only to the kind of level in question.

So, you can be level 100 in research skill from other sources, and still get all the training levels possible.

Room Effects

Rooms can now provide stats to faction members. So, I might add a Barracks room that adds combat stats per level, among various training types.

Teleport to Base and Respawn

Faction members can now teleport to the base pylon from anywhere. I may add spatial anomaly zones where teleportation isn’t possible, but that will probably be endgame content. :)

Teleporting home is free, and can’t be interrupted, so it’s a get out of trouble card. Since turns are simultaneous, however, you can teleport home and be killed simultaneously, so if you’re in trouble, you’ll need to get out before you’re at your last hit point. :)

The cost of teleporting home is lost time: wherever you were, you’ll have to find your way back normally.

Respawn works just like teleporting home, except you lose all your mana and equipped items. You also respawn at max HP.

I want the monsters to derive a benefit from whatever you drop, and I also want the player to be able to buy death protection for items and mana (with system currency, not faction currency).

Resource Node Changes

Resources nodes are now limited. This gives more incentive to explore the map, and find more resources to help build the faction base. Unlimited nodes are still possible, but if I use them, they’ll be in dangerous, distant zones. :)

I may also add harvestable nodes to the wilds (like the nodes in Hydroponics), where the resources are limited, but respawn.

Unique Items

Resource nodes now can drop unique items. These could be equipment your faction can’t make, or simply higher-level gear than your faction can currently make. These drops are non-random (you will always find X item at Y gather on Z node).

I want unique drops not only to be equippable, but also to be sellable to the faction for prestige, while benefiting the faction (say, by adding progress to a research). So if you find an item that doesn’t fit your build, you still have a fun option.

Note that while unique drops aren’t random, they’re all shared by whatever faction gatherers participated in the gather. So the quantity of unique drops might change per playthrough.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Itemization

Items now have item level. Each item is effectively a line of items, that will gain stats, abilities, and ability levels from item levels.

Faction item level is increased by the level of crafting projects and crafting rooms, and item level can also be upgraded at the pylon (presuming the faction has unlocked a higher item level).

I’d also like to add an investiture mechanic, to allow item customization via magic, but we’ll see. :)

Crafting Projects

Faction crafting projects run in room installations, and create items from raw materials. Item level is determined by the least of project level and room installation level.

Notes:

NPCs advance crafting projects.
The player can assist advancing crafting projects.
Raw materials do not have item level.
Crafting projects can only start if their product number in the shop is too low.
Crafting projects use raw mats from faction storage, which is filled by the player or NPCs gathering, usually in the wild, but sometimes on base (like harvesting in Hydroponics).
Crafted items can be purchased in the shop for prestige.


Room Installation Levels

Room level is determined by the number of upgrade construction projects completed on the room. I intend rooms to gain structure points, task slots, and other things via leveling, but for now, level acts as a crafting project gate.

Notes:

A construction project can be started if the room is not at max level. Max level is determined by research.
The faction has a limited number of construction tasks that can be started in parallel (I intend for this to increase via overall faction level).
I added a Builder NPC to advance room upgrades. :)


Research System

Faction research is repeatable. Every time a research completes, it levels up, and may do the following:

Unlock a new research line;
Unlock a new crafting project line;
Increase the max level of a faction room installation (allowing a construction task to upgrade room level);
Increase the level of an existing crafting project line;
And I may add more unlocks (such as path lines in the faction shop).


Note that for now, if crafting research or room construction completes during a crafting project, the item level is instantly advanced on the project (and on anything in faction storage).

I claim System shenanigans. :)

Priority System

The faction has a resource spending priority list for high-level decisions, split among the crafting rooms, construction, and research, each of which also has a priority list for spending decisions.

The lists will automatically adjust as tasks are started or skipped due to lack of resources. The player may also spend faction currency at the shop to increase the priority of projects on the lists.

Living Base

For all of the above, the idea is to have a “living” base, that the player can influence as a member (though not control outright).

I want the faction base to potentially develop quite differently in various playthroughs depending on player choice, so I’ll keep an eye on the auto-priority system, to make sure it doesn’t overly flatten the outcomes.

I'd also like to allow new room excavation and construction, with influenceable priorities for what is built, but we'll see. For now, the base will start with all rooms in place, and the question is what gets developed.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
More on Leveling

I implemented the following:
 System users (the player and faction NPCs) can now start with custom path levels, and NPCs can now level themselves with mana at the System pylon.
 Abilities can now level as described last week: via stacking from paths.
 Monsters now level by landing hits and participating in kills.
 Spawners now level by spawning monsters.
I can see expanding some of that, but for the demo, the above might be enough.

NPC Pathing

NPCs can now follow static routes, based on conditions and priorities. For instance, in my current test case, an Engineer will level up at the System pylon, travel to the Fabrication room if there’s an active task to work on, and if the work runs out, the Engineer will head back to the pylon.

I believe this will be most of the functionality I need to have a base alive with NPCs doing useful things. Outside the base, I intend faction NPC combat units to work like monsters, in which they make movement decisions based on their immediate circumstances. I’m also thinking that faction NPCs (and the player) will be able to teleport back to the base Pylon from anywhere.

That should prevent me from having to scale complex pathing algorithms to potentially thousands of units.

I also think the option to teleport home will make expeditions into the wild more like a dungeon run, where once you complete it, you just exit the dungeon. You'll need to decide for yourself when continuing is too risky, and whether you gained enough mana and killed enough monsters to justify jumping home for a resupply. :)

Faction Rooms and Tasks

I’ve decided that for faction task functions like the Research Lab, the room will be the thing (as opposed to a station in the room).

From the player’s perspective, this means that task actions like researching or crafting will be found under the zone area entry. It also means I won’t be adding scenic clutter to the target list (like research stations, tables, storage, and devices, that either don’t do anything, or only do one thing).

That will make it easier to level up rooms, without triggering the need to level up objects in it. While more textual scenery might be nice (and might be an interesting future expansion), it would also cost me more time to implement it, and I like the more efficient approach anyhow. :)

I also did the following:

 Task actions now display the task itself (instead of a fabrication task action label saying “work”, it might say “Rifle 1”).
 Rooms can now have multiple faction tasks running in parallel. I’d like to expand this to allow rooms to get more task slots as they level up.

Traits

To allow faction NPCs to choose which parallel task to work on, I implemented a prototype trait system. So, an Engineer with the “Flighty” trait will work on the newest task, while an Engineer with the “Steady” trait will work on the oldest. :)

Here's a screenshot of both Engineer types working:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/b8afcb3decb7555757396a5853e52e66e2a21c8a.png

I should be able to expand this system to allow for more interesting results from combat or pathing, and it would, of course, be nice to give the player a useful trait. :)

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Player Progression

Leveling

As reported last week, the player will have a prime level, which is the total of all path levels. Path levels are composed of mana levels, so ultimately it’s the total of all mana levels acquired that determine prime level.

Leveling prime, path, and mana will provide bonuses specific to each, which for now can include:


 Free attribute points
 Attribute and other stat awards
 Ability level awards
 Ability level choices
 Path unlock awards
 Path unlock choices
 Perk awards
 Perk choices


Paths have a max level, which you can fill with any arrangement of mana levels. This means the mana you use to level a path is build-determining, since different kinds of mana will unlock different stats, abilities, perks, and paths.

For the upcoming demo, I want to do two primary path trees, a mage tree focusing on innate spells, and a shooter tree focusing on magitech ranged weapons.

Note that stats can be repeating via X per Y levels, or a singleton at X level.

Leveling Dialog

I updated the leveling dialog to implement the above system. It now has an attribute pane, where you can add or remove free points, and a choice pane, where you can make selections based on the results of whatever mana level you raised for a path.

Here's a screen of its current status (content is not canonical!):

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45141288/9ab65698d4a222e861ac8bff11dbf43b6374a7de.png

Abilities

I’ve decided to change the leveling system for abilities, such that they'll gain their levels from the above process. That allows me to add more ability awards for leveling, since duplicates will now be valuable.

As abilities level, they’ll gain innate stat improvements. It’s possible I could work ability stat choices into the system, but I don’t think that will be needed for the demo.

Faction NPC Planning

For now, I’ve decided to build parallel path levels for NPCs, that improve on rails and don’t have choices. Adding leveling award decisions to NPCs could still happen in the future, and NPCs will likely get an algorithm to determine where they spend their available mana (based on a priority list).

Future Possibilities

Since I’m already tracking mana levels across all paths, I’m thinking that would be an interesting way to do more progression, such that you might get a stat boost like Fire Affinity for having fifty fire mana levels.

Again, I don’t think I’ll get this done for the demo, but I’d like to do it, and it should be straightforward. :)

I might even go so far as to grant awards for attribute milestones; the difficulty is that you might get attribute levels outside this process. I’d like to do it, but I still need to think on it.

Leveling at System Pylon

For now, I moved all leveling to the System Pylon, so you have to be in the base core to spend your mana on upgrades.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
Progression Design

Monsters vs. Users

I’m working on finalizing the primary leveling system. As it stands now, monsters and System users (the player and faction NPCs) won’t level the same way. This is thematic, since monsters don’t have the benefit of the sapient mana System.

 Users will spend mana to level paths, and the sum of all path levels will determine primary level.
 Monsters will only have a primary level, and will use kills and possibly things like infestation of resources to gain levels.
 Spawners will have a similar mechanic, in which they level up and in turn spawn higher-level monsters. They might use total spawns, total kills by spawn, infestations, and other metrics like that to gain progression.

Primary Level Effects

For monsters, the primary level will provide all relevant stats and ability unlocks. For users, it may be more limited to basic stats like max hit points (since paths cover the more exotic stats and abilities).

There could also be one-off stat increases at important levels (like 10 or 50).

Path Levels

Users level paths by spending mana. Paths have a specific set of mana that can be spent, so a Rogue path might use dark mana (shadows) or water mana (dexterity). Each mana type spent in a path provides its own base stats and ability or path unlocks. Each path level also provides its own stats.

So, in a Path of the Acolyte, spending Fire mana to level it might provide +1 strength attribute per level and eventually unlock the Fire Touch ability, a Fire Power perk, and the Path of the Fire Mage, whereas spending water mana might provide +1 dexterity, Ice Touch, Water Power, and Path of the Water Mage.

No matter what mana is used, however, each level of the Acolyte path would also provide +1 Intelligence, and ultimately unlock a generic path of the Mage, and possibly a generic ability.

Other thoughts:

 I’d like to provide free stats per level, allowing you to customize attribute gain.
 I’m toying with the idea of max path levels, forcing you to give up some unlocks, and I could also make it possible for only some paths to increase the primary level (which makes the system more class-like). I’d rather, however, try opportunity cost first.
 For NPCs, the primary level may look like a class. For instance, an NPC Engineer will have relevant paths, such as Path of Construction, that contribute to the level of the Engineer.

Mana Sources

Since mana is used both to level paths and power abilities, getting mana is an important mechanic. As it stands, I intend zones to have various levels of ambient mana, that can be absorbed passively or actively, depending on the System user’s mana affinities. So, an underground zone might have more dark and earth mana, while a desert zone might have more fire and light.

Monsters are another key source of mana. A Shadow Rat might drop dark mana, for instance. (I’d like this to matter to monsters, too, but we’ll see.)

Possibilities:

 I want the faction base to build rooms to absorb larger quantities of ambient mana (or even have things like planar taps), and then allow mana to be purchased for prestige, the faction currency.
 Another possibility are mana anomalies or veins that can hurt you if your resists or affinities are too low, but provide unparalleled absorption potential. (Monsters could leverage these too.)
 Unaspected or generic mana that could be refined into aspected mana. This would also allow more generic, weaker magic abilities (mana bolt instead of fire bolt). If I add it, unaspected mana would probably be the most common. Lesser paths might use it as upgrade fuel.

Game Loop

The player will suit up at base, go into the wilds, kill monsters, and absorb mana. If the player survives, the mana can be taken back to the base to use for upgrades at the System pylon.

Notes:

 At this point, there are no max mana stats, but I’m thinking I’ll want that, to make the game loop more interesting.
 I want one of the potential purchases at the System pylon to be mana protection, so that if you buy X protection for a mana type, you get to keep X mana if you die (instead of it being looted by whatever killed you).
 Note that right now the base will have minimal but comprehensive ambient mana sources (which I intend to also be an upgrade project, so you could increase base ambience, if you wanted). The idea is that you’ll want a way to get at least a little fuel for abilities if you’ve died and respawned with nothing.

Other changes

I updated equipment such that it’s now possible to fully-reconfigure a loadout in one turn (previously, equipped gear could only be unequipped, not transferred to other valid slots, so it took two turns to transfer it).

I also did low-level updates on the stat and character systems, to prepare for implementing the above leveling systems, and I tested monsters with levels that make them stronger.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
World Interface Changes


 Did more color improvements to targets pane, to help distinguish varying kinds of information.
 Consolidated these zone stats to targets pane: cover, concealment, ambient mana, terrain type and difficulty, and searched status.
 Consolidated these player stats to target pane: mana, mana regen, stamina, force field, alteration, and evasion (most stats also included for now for NPCs and monsters).
 Reorganized left and right information panes to fill in the newly-available space.
 Resized the modal action dialogs.

Scouting Update

Previously, actions would accumulate disturbance, which decayed slowly and stuck with characters wherever they went. I’m now trying a flatter system, where each action provides disturbance for a single turn.

So, you can be spotted one turn, and if you do something less obvious, you can hide (as can NPCs/monsters).

Note that disturbance (and detection) can physical or magical.

Equipment and Path Dialogs

I changed the equipment and path dialogs to use the new inline action pane layout. This means all possible actions are visible at-a-glance, instead of requiring a lot of clicking to reveal.

I still need to do more color work, and probably more fundamental rework, but I’m liking how it’s looking so far.
